why: Same-day flaky-test fix (0036), in next/, stacked on pull request 1366. The law 'Q9/Q12 the assembled door refuses before an envelope, binding, reply or local step is saved' in next/apps/fabrika/src/runtime-recovery.laws.integration.test.ts went red in about 0.4% of full runs when a run crossed an hour. The objects' runtimes are built in product code (projectRuntime, then project in next/packages/libfabrika/src/cloudflare/runtime.ts) with Effect's default Clock, which reads Date.now(); no layer seam lets a test give them Effect's TestClock, which @effect/vitest gives only to the test fiber. So the law now pins the wall clock inside one hour with vitest's fake Date (toFake Date only, shouldAdvanceTime true), set to the top of SENT's hour and acquired in the run's scope with Effect.acquireRelease, as build-one-file.integration.test.ts already does with vi.setSystemTime. No retry, no assertion changed, no product file changed.
note: Proof 1, base head 36db10a81c3a8e0a1a833b7f09effb7714073485 plus this change (committed as the head this row lands in): `nice -n 15 pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3 next/apps/fabrika/src/runtime-recovery.laws.integration.test.ts` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13)'. The same command at the base head before the change also passed 13 of 13. Proof 2, a throwaway harness in the scratchpad (never committed): a script copied the old law (git show HEAD) and the new law into two temporary test files beside the real one, patched the real Date.now with an offset, set it 30 s before the next hour boundary at the top of each property run and LEAD ms before the boundary just before refusal 1 (each jump under the 60 s quota window), and ran each with `nice -n 15 pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3 next/apps/fabrika/src/zz-harness-<old|new>.laws.integration.test.ts -t "Q9/Q12"`. LEAD 3 ms: old -> 'Tests 1 failed | 12 skipped (13)', 'Failure: AssertionError: expected { program: { writes: 16, …(1) }, …(2) } to deeply equal { program: { writes: 15, …(1) }, …(2) }' at the localUsage check after the refusal row counts; new -> 'Tests 1 passed | 12 skipped (13)'. LEAD 1 ms and 10 ms gave the same pair. So at this head the crossing shows as one extra local write, not a second sums row: sums stayed at 0 rows in both stores through every refusal in a debug run. A first harness that jumped the clock up to an hour turned the refusal into an accept because the quota window is 60 s; that harness was wrong and its result is not used. The temporary files were deleted and git status showed only the law file.
